newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says U.S. pledged to provide food aid.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says U.S. pledged to provide food aid.

text.p: The United States has pledged to ease a trade embargo against North Korea and give food aid to the flood-ravaged communist state, Pyongyang's official news agency said on Monday.
Washington struck the deals during talks in New York between officials from the United States and North Korea from December 9-29, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
"The U.S. side promised that it would take additional measures to ease the embargo on the DPRK (North Korea) and supply food to the DPRK," KCNA said in a dispatch monitored in Tokyo.
On Sunday, North Korea apologised for the first time for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korea in September, expressing "deep regret" in a brief statement.

The statement was issued after intense bargaining in New York between U.S. and North Korean officials on a choice of words to make the apology acceptable to Seoul, which branded the incursion a "military provocation".

U.S. President Bill Clinton on Sunday welcomed North Korea's apology, saying it was a "significant development, which I hope will contribute to the reduction of tensions on the Korean peninsula". Reclusive North Korea has been suffering from famine after two consecutive years of serious flooding.
